chances.title: About 4 in 10 got in, in state or not.

lede.s: 72,933 students applied for fall 2025. 30,446 got in. Washington students got in only a little more often than out-of-state students, so where you live isn't the whole story. The rest of this page is.
lede.p: 72,933 students applied for fall 2025. 30,446 got in. Washington students got in only a little more often than out-of-state students, so where your student lives isn't the whole story. The rest of this page is.

grids.aria: About 46 of 100 dots filled: 45.7% of Washington applicants were admitted
About 42 of 100 dots filled: 42.2% of out-of-state applicants were admitted

chances.src: Fall 2025 first-years (C1): Washington 6,980 of 15,260 admitted (45.7%). Out of state 18,813 of 44,619 (42.2%). International 4,653 of 13,054 (35.6%). Overall 30,446 of 72,933 (41.7%).

ladder.title: 4 things are top-tier. Your essay is one of them.
ladder.lede: By senior fall, your classes and GPA are mostly set. Your essay is the top-tier piece you can still change before Nov 15.
important: First in your family to go to college
not_considered: How often you toured or emailed
ladder.note: Top tier = where your hours go before Nov 15 ↓
ladder.src: Section C7, first-year admission factors, 2025–26 Common Data Set.

numbers.lede: Type your GPA on a 4.0 scale to see where it sits next to UW's first-years. This is a range, not a cutoff.

gpa.default: Average GPA of enrolled first-years: 3.84 on a 4.0 scale.
gpa.near: Right around UW's average. Now your top-tier rows decide it: how hard your classes were, and your essay.
gpa.above: Above UW's average. Good start. Your classes and your essay still do the heavy lifting.
gpa.below: Below UW's average. That's not a no. Your essay is top-tier too, and it's the piece you can still change. Put your hours there.

facts.text: of enrolled first-years had a GPA of 3.75 or higher (18% had a 4.0).

numbers.src: Sections C11–C12: enrolled first-years, fall 2025 (99.9% reported a GPA). UW rates test scores and class rank "not considered" (C7).

dates.title: One deadline. No early round at UW.

kicker.s: Send this part to your parents

money.title: If you qualify for aid, UW meets about 74% of need on average.
money.lede: The sticker price isn't your price. The net price calculator gives your family a real estimate in about 15 minutes.
money.aid_line: About 1 in 3 first-years get need-based grants. The average need-based package is $22,538 a year.
money.src: Sections G1 (2026–27 tuition and required fees) and H2, 2025–26 Common Data Set. On-campus food and housing (about $18,405) cost extra.

todo.title: 4 moves, all aimed at UW's top tier.

items.title: Read your essay out loud.
items.body: UW uses your Common App essay, and essays are top-tier here. If a sentence could be about anyone, cut it.

items.title: Check your courses against your transcript.
items.body: UW has you type in every class and grade yourself. Match it line by line. Your classes and GPA are top-tier.

items.title: Pick your first-choice major on purpose.
items.body: If your major admits students directly, it has to be your first choice to count. Add a second choice too.

items.title: Put a number on every activity.
items.body: Hours a week, people you led, what changed because of you.

todo.done: All 4 done. That's a real application. ✓

title.s: Is your essay doing its job?
title.p: Is your student's essay doing its job?

lede.s: Your essay is top-tier at UW, and it's the only essay UW asks for. Here's what I looked for as an admissions reader. Read your essay, then tap what's true.
lede.p: The essay is top-tier at UW, and it's the only essay UW asks for. Here's what I looked for as an admissions reader. Read your student's essay together, then tap what's true.

items.title: It answers the exact question asked.
items.body: Circle the key words in the prompt. Every paragraph should answer them, not a question close to them.

items.title: Only one person could have written it.
items.body: Swap in a friend's name. If it still works, it isn't specific enough yet.

items.title: It shows one real moment.
items.body: A scene beats a list of awards. The list already lives in the activities section.

items.title: A reader could sum it up in one line.
items.body: Readers spend a few minutes per file. Hand them the sentence they'll repeat when they argue for you.

after.s: Not sure you can check all four? That's normal. It's hard to judge your own essay.
after.p: Not sure? That's normal. It's hard to judge an essay you're close to.

self_check.all_done: All 4. Nice work. A fresh reader can still catch what you can't see.

take.heading: What I saw as an admissions reader
take.quote: When three out of four first-years have a 3.75 or higher, grades stop telling readers apart. Your essay is where a reader finally meets you, and at UW it's the only one. Make it one real moment that only you could write.
